subject: Cost map & pilot decision path
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@payriva.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: cost map + recommended pilot decision path

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on the pain, goals, and what a minimum pilot would need to show. Happy to jump back on a call to walk through any of the numbers.

Pain / goal highlights (what you told us)
- High volume of short verification & routing prompts: ~1.2M prompt calls / month across verification and routing flows, ~15 tokens prompt on average, responses ~45 tokens.
- Current infra cost and latency spikes during peaks (>95th percentile latency >600ms) causing NPS/CSAT drops for support flows.
- Primary product goal: reduce unit cost by 3–4x while keeping P95 latency under 250ms for routing/verification flows.

Token-econ quick sketch
- Baseline (current vendor): ~0.12 USD / 1k tokens -> ~1080 USD / month in token charges for the sample workload (this is illustrative; we’ll refine with logs).
- Two levers we discussed that materially change the economics: batching + prefix/KV caching. With continuous batching for short requests and a 30–40% cache hit rate on repeated verification prompts, our model shows unit cost reductions of 2.8x–3.6x.

Recommended pilot (scope & goals)
- Scope: 30-day pilot on Dedicated pool for the verification/routing flow only (target traffic mirror at 20–30% of production).
- Success criteria: measured token cost reduction >=2.5x, sustained P95 latency <=300ms, no functional regressions on 1000 prompt test set.
- Budget anchor: pilot monthly run (20–30% traffic) estimated at $12k–$22k net (inclusive of tokens + reserved capacity) depending on achieved cache hit and batching efficiency. Full-production extrapolation (if pilot results match) shows annualized unit cost roughly consistent with the 3x reduction target.

Next steps / asks
1) Can you share a 7–14 day sample of request logs (anonymized) so we can produce a model with your real prompt/token distribution? The pilot econ above is a working estimate; sample logs will tighten it.
2) Decision owner: confirm who on your side signs pilot budget (we discussed Hannah and the head of platform) and an expected procurement timeline.
3) Proposed dates: pilot kickoff week of Oct 4 -> initial readout ~Nov 4.

I attached a short pilot scope workbook that breaks the assumptions and shows the sensitivity to cache hit and batch size.

Attachments: payriva-pilot-scope.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with a one-pager and proposed SLOs once we get the logs.

— Priya

From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@payriva.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:11:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap: cost map + recommended pilot decision path

Priya —

Thanks for the clear recap, this is very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Latency / SLOs: for routing flows the business requires P95 < 250ms but we can tolerate P99 up to ~500ms if cost benefits are material. Can Redwood guarantee a regional SLO or do you need a Dedicated pool per region?
2) Logs: we can export anonymized request logs by Tuesday (Sep 16). Format will be newline-delimited JSON with timestamp, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, flow_id. Is that format OK?
3) Pilot billing: finance prefers a capped pilot spend with a go/no-go at 30 days. Can you provide a capped estimate and an overage mechanism?

We’re also curious about how batching affects tail latency for these short calls — if you have a short write-up on the batching profile you saw in similar customers, that’d help with the internal cost/ops discussion.

I’ll loop in Jay (head of platform) once we have the logs and a capped estimate.

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah —

Appreciate the quick responses. Answers inline and next steps: 

> Can Redwood guarantee a regional SLO or do you need a Dedicated pool per region?
We recommend a single Dedicated pool in your primary region for the pilot (US-East). That configuration gives the most predictable latency and cost for a short pilot. For production, multi-region routing + automatic fallback is straightforward; we’ll propose a low-complexity multi-region plan if you decide to expand.

> Logs format
Newline-delimited JSON with timestamp, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, flow_id works great. Please exclude any PII; an anonymized id for user/session is fine.

> Capped pilot billing
We can provide a capped pilot estimate. Ben and Marissa are preparing a capped low/high cost table with a suggested 10% buffer and an overage rate that is pre-agreed (per-token at our hosted rate above the cap). I’ll include the capped numbers in the pilot one-pager I’m attaching.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-onepager.pdf (pdf)

Proposed next call: Thu, Sep 16 at 10:00 AM ET to confirm logs format and decision owner. If that works for you I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Priya
